A metal film of 100 nm can enter the model as a volume of that thickness or as
a sheet of zero thickness. An *approximation profile* makes that choice for
every film of the stack and says what happens to the heights above it. A
Palace simulation chooses its profile with `set_route`; an AEDT request with
`modeling`. [Route A and Route B](../../concepts/routes.qmd) explains when to
use which; this page gives each profile's exact effect.

## The profiles {#profiles}

Take a 100 nm aluminium film on a 500 µm silicon substrate: silicon from
z = −500 to 0 µm, the film from 0 to 0.1 µm, vacuum above. The five profiles
are distinct; none is another's alias.

| Profile | Route | The film becomes | Heights above the film | Chosen by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `route_b` | B | A 0.1 µm volume whose surface is a perfect conductor; its inside is left out of the mesh | Unchanged | Palace `set_route("B")`, the default |
| `thin_film` | A | A sheet at z = 0, where the film sits | Move down by 0.1 µm | Palace `set_route("A")`; AEDT `modeling="thin_film"` |
| `substrate_face` | A | A sheet on the substrate face you bind it to, z = 0 | Unchanged | Palace `set_route("A", approximation_profile=...)` |
| `metal_gap_equivalent` | A | For two facing films of a flip-chip, a sheet on each substrate face; both thicknesses are removed | Move down by each film's thickness | Palace `set_route("A", approximation_profile=...)` |
| `solid` | C | A 0.1 µm volume kept in the model | Unchanged | AEDT `modeling="solid"` |

For a flip-chip the difference shows in the gap. With a 0.1 µm film on each die,
a bottom substrate face at z = 0, a top substrate face at z = 10.2 µm and
10.0 µm of vacuum between the films:

| Profile | Bottom sheet | Top sheet | Sheet-to-sheet gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| `thin_film` | z = 0 | z = 10.0 | 10.0 µm, the metal-to-metal gap |
| `substrate_face` | z = 0 | z = 10.2 | 10.2 µm, the substrate-to-substrate gap |
| `metal_gap_equivalent` | z = 0 | z = 10.0 | 10.0 µm, the metal-to-metal gap |

`thin_film` removes every film of the stack; `metal_gap_equivalent` removes
exactly the two facing films you bind, one attached at its lower face and one
at its upper face, on two different substrates. Bumps and posts stay volumes
in every profile; their ends move with the heights. The outlines, holes,
materials and Net names are the same in all of them.

These heights were computed with SCGSim's own mapping
(`scgsim.geometry.interpret_physical_layers`) for declarations of these films.

## Palace: `set_route` {#palace-caller-profile}

`ElectrostaticSim` and `EigenmodeSim` choose the profile with `set_route()`,
before `mesh()`. One call states the whole setting: it replaces the route and
the profile together.

| Call | Profile used |
|---|---|
| `set_route("B")`, or no call | `route_b` |
| `set_route("A")` | `thin_film` |
| `set_route("A", approximation_profile=profile)` | `substrate_face` or `metal_gap_equivalent`, with their bindings |

A face profile names, for each film, the dielectric Entity it lies on and that
Entity's face:

```python
from scgsim.geometry.models.physical import ApproximationProfile

profile = ApproximationProfile(
    name="substrate_face",
    revision="v1",
    parameters={"film_bindings": authored_film_bindings},
)
sim.set_route("A", approximation_profile=profile)
```

`authored_film_bindings` maps each declared physical layer ID to exactly
`supporting_entity_id` (a dielectric Entity) and `supporting_side` (`"upper"`
or `"lower"`), for example
`{"D0_M1": {"supporting_entity_id": "D0_SUB", "supporting_side": "upper"}}`.
`substrate_face` takes one or two bindings; `metal_gap_equivalent` exactly two,
on two different substrates facing each other. A missing or wrong binding is
refused before any native work, with the call shape to use.

`input_summary()` shows the route and the profile, the default included. A
profile the plan's films do not fit (Route A with `route_b` or `solid`, Route B
with `thin_film`) is refused when `mesh()` builds, not at `set_route()`. The
Surface-EPR films stay the plan's, `plan.set_surface_epr(specs)`, whatever the
profile.

## AEDT: `modeling` {#aedt-modeling}

An HFSS or Q3D request uses `thin_film` for `modeling="thin_film"` and `solid`
for `modeling="solid"`; [AEDT: solid or thin_film](aedt-runtime.qmd#aedt-solid-thin-film)
shows the heights. Q2D takes its own cross-section and no profile.

## Where the declarations come from {#declarations}

[]{#typed-source-carrier-and-plan}[]{#selected-declarations-and-source-incidence}[]{#fresh-and-historical-layer-records}The
profiles read the physical declaration of each layer of the PDK's stack:
whether it is a film of the stack, a local film or a finite volume, its
material, thickness and the face it is attached at. The PDK writes them;
a notebook does not. How a PDK author writes them, and which older records are
refused, is in [GeometryPlan internals](../../contribute/internals/geometry-plan.qmd#physical-declarations).
